ingredients.name: Copper Tripeptide-1
ingredients.description: A copper-linked peptide used to help keep skin in good condition.
ingredients.knownLimitations: Its presence identifies a copper-peptide ingredient. It does not tell us the results you will get from the whole serum.

education.summary: A copper-linked peptide used to help keep skin in good condition.

whatItIs.text: A short peptide joined to copper. This is an ingredient name, not a quality score.

purpose.text: Used as a skin-conditioning ingredient: a broad cosmetic role concerned with skin condition and appearance.

evidence.text: The CIR assessment addresses specified cosmetic identities, uses and concentrations. It is a safety assessment, not a trial showing that a finished serum reduces wrinkles. A full topical efficacy review remains pending.
evidence.label: Safety assessment

precautions.text: Cosmetic safety conclusions do not extend to injection. FDA separately identifies limited human safety data and potential immune-response risks for compounded injectable GHK-Cu.

education.takeaway: Its presence identifies a copper-peptide ingredient. It does not tell us the results you will get from the whole serum.

ingredients.name: Acetyl Hexapeptide-8
ingredients.description: A peptide studied for the appearance of expression lines around the eyes.
ingredients.knownLimitations: There is human research on a preparation of this ingredient. That is different from a direct test of finished products containing this ingredient.

education.summary: A peptide studied for the appearance of expression lines around the eyes.

whatItIs.text: A synthetic peptide investigated under the name Argireline. The study concerns a specific preparation, not every product listing this ingredient.

purpose.text: Studied as a cosmetic ingredient for reducing the appearance of eye-area lines.

evidence.text: A four-week randomized placebo-controlled trial enrolled 60 Chinese participants (3:1 allocation) and reported improved eye-area wrinkle measures. The inspected abstract does not establish results for the retail serums here or long-term benefit. A 24-hour laboratory skin-penetration study is a different kind of evidence, not a clinical efficacy trial.
evidence.label: Ingredient study

precautions.text: The 2025 safety panel concluded safe cosmetic use up to 0.005%; above that, it found insufficient data to determine safety. This is not evidence of harm above that amount. The pure-peptide concentrations in these compared serums are not verified, so this assessment cannot certify either bottle. A commercial blend percentage is not automatically the pure-peptide percentage.

education.takeaway: There is human research on a preparation of this ingredient. That is different from a direct test of finished products containing this ingredient.
